web_evidence.title: GRETIL accented Śaunaka saṃhitā
web_evidence.use: Direct repeated bare root attestation and accent/role slots. Retains m before the following vowel in the second accusative.

web_evidence.title: Vedic Heritage Portal Śaunaka saṃhitā 11.3
web_evidence.addresses: Second paryāya of 11.3, corresponding to 32–49 in Whitney
web_evidence.use: Devanāgarī corroboration of the 18 occurrences. In 4.5 the predicative form is written अजीगमम्.

web_evidence.title: Śaunaka 11.3.36 pada transcription
web_evidence.use: Separates pra before first verb and separates the two instrumentals and accusatives. Exact local pada witness, same-recension corroboration.

web_evidence.title: TITUS Śaunaka, 11.3 second paryāya
web_evidence.use: Same caṅ form with preceding accusative transcribed enaṃ where GRETIL has enam. Keep representation distinction.

web_evidence.title: W. D. Whitney, revised C. R. Lanman, Atharva-Veda Saṃhitā, HOS 8 (1905)
web_evidence.use: Takes bare verb causatively with the dish and reports only a detailed-different Paippalāda XVI parallel. Notice of the edition difference in 34 is local to the instrument.

web_evidence.title: Kṣemakaraṇadāsa Trivedi, Atharvavedabhāṣya, electronic presentation with named authorship
web_evidence.addresses: 11.3.32 pāda notes to ajīgamam and 11.3.36 running gloss
web_evidence.use: Explicit svārtha-ṇic, luṅ and caṅ, with attainment gloss. Do not attribute this to Sāyaṇa.

web_evidence.title: Kāśikā 1.4.52
web_evidence.use: Counterfactual base movement subject becomes karman with ṇic in W.

web_evidence.title: Kāśikā 3.1.26
web_evidence.use: Causal ṇic for the independently supplied hetumat reading only.

web_evidence.title: Kāśikā 1.4.42
web_evidence.use: Instrument is the supplied means of realizing the action.

observation_units: Śaunaka second-paryāya null-preverb refrain with 18 addresses, one source series
Whitney's local causal analysis and subject/theme interpretation
Trivedi's individually attributed svārtha-ṇic and attainment reading
decision: Accept the bare P1sg token series and preserve the causal-role and svārtha analyses under separate source labels. Neither the word spelling nor its three instrumental numbers can supply a second independent finite paradigm.
